context:
Goal: main stays green and the records page stays current.
Problem (rule): a merge by GitHub's button or by auto-merge skips merge.py's records rebuild. The page goes stale, and --check turns main red. No hook refuses either.
Based on (record): docs/decisions/no-merge-during-batch-ci.md lines 33-35.
Departs from: main, where a button merge can leave the page stale. Each option closes that gap a different way.

options.gain: Claude cannot cause a stale page.
options.label: A hook refuses enable_pr_auto_merge, and the decision says the button is yours only (recommended)
A bot push rebuilds the page on main after any merge
Waive --check on runs that are not from a PR

reply: Lane notes-keep-reverify, 14:48 CST, on "is B the best option?": b covers the most, since it also covers your own button presses, but it costs the most. A bot commits straight to main, against PR-only main, so it needs your exception and a branch-protection bypass, plus one extra commit and CI run per merge, and a race when two merges land close together. A safer b: the bot opens a rebuild PR, which the batch runner merges. a is one small guard rule that stops Claude causing the gap, but not your own presses. How often a button merge happens is unmeasured. The lane recommends a, unless you press the button yourself often; then the PR form of b. Pick a, b or c.
short: Button merge: refuse auto-merge, bot rebuild, or waive the check
title: How should a merge by GitHub's button stop leaving the records page stale?
